Subject: Post-call: MidCity Bank evals & next steps (dataset format + scoring)

Hi Sonia / Rajiv —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps to get MidCity running customer-specific evals on Redwood: 

1) Primary goal: Verify model fit for customer-facing transaction summarization & smart-reply in the MidCity mobile app.
2) Recommended models to evaluate (fast win + quality):
   - llama-2-13b-chat (instruction-tuned) — good balance of latency and quality for smaller prompts
   - mosaic-mistral-7b-instruct — strong instruction-following, good token efficiency
   - redwood-instruct-3b (quantized) — lowest-cost baseline for throughput tests

3) Evaluation plan (high level):
   - We will run a set of 2k representative examples from your sample dataset (see attached eval_dataset_sample.csv) through the three models.
   - Scoring rubric: accuracy of extracted entities (transaction amount, merchant), fluency/readability (human-rated sample), and safety/regulatory flags (PII masking).
   - Target metrics: >95% entity extraction recall, mean quality score >=4/5 on human evals for summaries.

4) Infrastructure/setup notes:
   - We’ll run the evals on a dedicated Redwood eval project to ensure reproducibility (model versions pinned, seed control).
   - Dev will provide the dataset format spec and a script to ingest CSV/JSONL into Redwood eval harness.

5) Next actions:
   - Sonia: confirm you can share a 2k example subset by EOD Thu 4/1 (PII redacted or tokenized as needed).
   - Rajiv: confirm any special scoring weights (e.g., prioritize merchant recall over summary length).
   - We (Neha + Dev): will provision the eval project and send instructions + a sample scoring template.

Attachments: eval_dataset_sample.csv (sample rows, schema), redwood_eval_instructions.pdf (format + scoring template).

Link to shared plan: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_midcity-eval-plan

Happy to hop on a quick follow-up if useful — suggested slot Thu 11am PT.

Best,

Hi Sonia — great questions. Quick answers: 

1) Token format: <ACC_XXXX> is fine — we commonly accept any consistent placeholder. Please include a mapping CSV if you need us to reverse-map for internal analytics (we can keep that mapping encrypted).

2) Checklist support: yes — we’ll run automated scoring (entity F1, token-level PII detection, rouge/bleu for surface match where applicable) and a human checklist sample. Our evaluation harness supports attaching a 5–7 question checklist per example and aggregating pass/fail metrics.

I’ve attached redwood_eval_instructions.pdf with the dataset schema (CSV/JSONL accepted) and the sample checklist template. 

We’ll provision the eval project today and send you the ingestion script (csv_to_eval.py) and a link to a sandbox project in Redwood. Expect that from Dev in the next email.

Hi Rajiv / Sonia —

Yes to both. Technical notes for the eval run: 

1) Sandbox provisioning: I’ve created a sandbox project "midcity-eval-sandbox" in Redwood and pinned the following model versions for parity:
   - llama-2-13b-chat@2027-02-15 (float16)
   - mosaic-mistral-7b-instruct@2027-01-12 (float16)
   - redwood-instruct-3b@2026-11-03 (q4_0)

2) Latency/cost telemetry:
   - We’ll capture p50/p95 latency and token cost per 1k tokens for each run. Expect p95 latency approx: llama-2-13b-chat ~420ms, mistral-7b ~310ms, redwood-instruct-3b (q4) ~200ms on the sandbox GPU profile (A100-like). These are estimates — we’ll report observed values in the sandbox run.

3) Scoring template: the ingest pipeline accepts a JSONL of examples with fields: id, prompt, ground_truth, metadata. We’ll attach the sample csv_to_eval.py script that converts your CSV to the JSONL schema. The scoring pipeline accepts custom weights (we’ll use merchant=0.5, amount=0.3, readability=0.2 as you requested).

4) Running the run: once you share the 2k subset, we’ll run the automated pass and a stratified human checklist of 200 examples. Turnaround target: 3 business days for raw automated metrics, 5 business days including human review.
